stem:
Ira writes four claims about the number list 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, …

Which claim treats the list as a mathematical pattern?

options.text: The list looks neat, so it is a pattern even with no rule stated.
The list is a pattern of adding 1, because whole numbers always grow by 1.
Each term is 2 more than the one before, because we keep adding 2.
The same list also proves a new theorem about all infinite sequences.

teacher.key_rationale: A pattern claim needs a visible regularity and a reason it continues. Adding 2 each time is that pair. Looking neat omits the rule. Adding 1 is the counting-number rule, not this list. A theorem about all infinite sequences over-extends the claim.
